title: workspace-runtime generates a claude agent file for each authored `@agent-profile`, or reports why it does not
summary: @inventarch/workspace-runtime adds the ./internal/generate subpath, which exports generateAgentProfiles(reader, within, host) with the GeneratedFile, GeneratedSet, GeneratedWord and UnsupportedRecord types. It returns a frozen {files, unsupported}. Only `@agent-profile` records at band 100 (authored by the workspace) that the scope token admits are read, by identity; one below band 100, where an installed or adopted base places the public vocabulary, renders nothing and is not reported, and a workspace that authors public systems renders their profiles. For codex every authored profile is an unsupported row {identity, word: 'agent-profile', reason}, because a codex agent needs an entry in .codex/config.toml, which holds the owned MCP block. For claude each profile renders {path, text, identity, word: 'agent-profile'} at .claude/agents/<profile name>.md, except that a profile is an unsupported row naming the reason, and the others still render, when its name is not a portable host name (lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens, a letter first and no hyphen last, at most 64 characters, no Windows device name including com0 and lpt0), when its capabilities allow no host tool (claude gives an agent with no tool list every tool, so no file is written), when the composition compiler would refuse its capability closure (its capabilities include one another in a cycle, or an included capability has an effect its includer does not declare), or when its text is not inert prose (no executable dynamic context such as !`cmd`, no active HTML, no unbalanced code span or fence), which is judged on each authored value before it is rendered, so the reason names what the record itself holds, and again on the rendered file. A profile's capability closure is its composition.capabilities and every capability they include through composition.includes, each once. The text is YAML frontmatter (the JSON-quoted name; a description taken from the meaning.says of its composition.agent when the workspace authors that agent, otherwise the profile's own; and tools, the claude names of the host tools the effects of the profile's own composition.capabilities cover through the prose profiles' effect table, where read covers Read, Glob and Grep and no other effect maps a tool, as one comma-separated string; the compiler holds each capability's own effects as the ceiling of what it includes, so the included capabilities add no tool), then the marker `<!-- Generated by ia project; edit the cited native records. -->` on its own line, then a body naming the profile and its agent, with a Mandate section, a Voice section when composition.voice is set, a Tools section with one line per capability of the closure naming its operations, effects and host tools, and a Delegates section with one line per composition.delegates reference. The Mandate section holds the profile's own composition.mandate as one list item with its authority fields (participant, moves, scope, excluded words, covers) and execution.limit-* fields nested beneath it, as authored; when that mandate names a participant other than the profile's agent, a nested line says so, and that the edit guard and the CLI's mandate profile judge the agent by the mandates that bind it. A profile that names no mandate falls back to the authored mandates @inventarch/runtime's governingMandates says bind its composition.agent (those that name it, and those that name no participant and state a scope or covers; one that states neither governs no path and is left out), each as such a group under a line labelling them as the fallback and saying the guard refuses the agent where a mandate that binds another participant governs and none of these grants the move; the line says when none binds, and says the fallback is unavailable, with the reason, when a mandate's authority cannot be read or the agent is not admitted, without failing the render; the fallback is resolved only for a rendered profile that needs it. Free text is written as the position packet writes it: on one line, each bare IA word a code span in the body, C0 and C1 controls, Unicode line separators and bidirectional controls as spaces, `<!--` written `<!--`, a `!` that a rendered code span would follow written `!`, and a leading `<` written `<`, so no value opens a comment, reads as dynamic context or opens an HTML block. A reference no admitted record in the scope answers is printed as authored, and the agent, mandate, voice and capability lines, whose records' fields would be read, say it is not admitted in this scope (a delegate, an operation and a participant are printed as authored only). The bytes depend only on the records: no absolute path, time, scope token or revision. An unknown host is refused with IA-PROJECTION-INPUT-INVALID, and for either host an unknown or stale scope token keeps its database code. Limits: the frontmatter names no model; conditional field values are not rendered.
